title: The Growth Kinetic and Ultra High Hardness of CoCrFeNiTi High–Entropy Alloy by Mechanical Alloying and Spark Plasma Sintering

recollection.starting_material: Guess: Equiatomic elemental powders of Co, Cr, Fe, Ni, and Ti (≥99.5% purity), mixed as a high-entropy alloy feed for mechanical alloying.
recollection.intervention: Guess: High-energy mechanical alloying (planetary milling under Ar, ball-to-powder ratio ~10:1, 20–40 h, small PCA), to produce a nanocrystalline/supersaturated solid solution powder; followed by spark plasma sintering at ~800–950 °C under ~40–60 MPa for 5–10 minutes with isothermal holds at several temperatures to extract grain growth kinetics.
recollection.structure: Guess: Near-full-density, nanocrystalline, multiphase HEA with a dominant FCC (CoCrFeNi-rich) matrix containing B2-ordered (Ni,Co)Ti-rich precipitates and/or BCC domains; occasional σ/Laves-type intermetallics; mean crystallite/grain size on the order of ~50–150 nm after SPS (smaller after MA, slight coarsening upon SPS).
recollection.mechanism: Guess: Ultra-high hardness arises from combined Hall–Petch strengthening (nanograins), severe solid-solution lattice distortion, and dispersion strengthening by hard B2/Laves intermetallics; sluggish diffusion plus Zener pinning retards grain growth during SPS. Grain growth controlled by boundary diffusion with a growth exponent near 2 and an apparent activation energy in the ~170–220 kJ/mol range.
recollection.results: Guess: Relative density ≥98–99%; Vickers hardness ~1200–1600 HV (≈12–16 GPa) depending on SPS temperature/hold (highest at the finest grain sizes); nanoindentation hardness up to ~14–16 GPa; grain growth exponent n ≈ 2; activation energy for grain growth Q ~180±40 kJ/mol; modest grain coarsening with increasing SPS temperature; possible compressive strength in the ~2–3 GPa range for the densified nanostructured condition.

score.note: The recollection identifies mechanical alloying under argon followed by brief SPS, but gives substantially incorrect milling durations and sintering conditions. It correctly anticipates a nanocrystalline, FCC-dominant multiphase structure, though it misses the 83% FCC/17% BCC split and adds unsupported intermetallics. The core Hall–Petch, solid-solution, and milling-induced strengthening mechanisms are correctly identified, despite speculative additions. Quantitative hardness is far too high, and the reported phase fractions, 675 HV hardness, 1894 MPa compressive strength, and 1238 MPa yield stress are not recalled.
